subject.title: exec auto-reviewer re-bills a fresh model completion for every byte-identical repeated exec

question: Should OpenClaw approve a bounded per-reviewer exact-input cache for model-backed exec reviewer decisions, and what cache lifetime/key/outcome scope is acceptable on the exec approval boundary?
rationale: The bug and likely fix boundary are clear, but skipping a fresh model review for a later identical exec request changes security-review semantics and needs explicit maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve exact-input per-run memo
options.body: Cache only within the shared reviewer instance using the full reviewed input or prompt, keep the cache bounded, and preserve allow-once host semantics.

options.title: Narrow cached outcomes
options.body: Cache only parsed low-risk allow-once decisions while keeping ask, timeout, and error outcomes fresh for a smaller approval-boundary change.

options.title: Keep fresh review semantics
options.body: Reject memoization for now and accept repeated reviewer cost to preserve one model review per exec request.

recommendation.title: Approve exact-input per-run memo
recommendation.body: Cache only within the shared reviewer instance using the full reviewed input or prompt, keep the cache bounded, and preserve allow-once host semantics.
